verdicts.reason: Both just shrink the original into a strip: the CTA has turned into a small chip at the start of the flavour row, the chip labels are only a few px tall and can't be read, the flavour order is shuffled, and the legal line is squeezed into a tiny block beside the chips. A at least gives balanced left-product / centre-text / right-legal zones, while B jams the legal block right against the can at the right edge and leaves the left side empty.

Near-identical layouts with the can on the right. The CTA is no bigger than the chips, the chip text is illegible, and the legal copy is squeezed into a narrow column of microscopic text. In A that column butts against the last chip and runs almost to the bottom edge. In B it is jammed against the can instead, but the chip row is spaced slightly more evenly, so B is marginally less bad.

A puts the can, the legal block and the end of the chip row together on the right, so that corner is overcrowded and the left is empty. B spreads the weight better with the can on the left. Both share the same fatal issues: the CTA is reduced to an unreadable chip, the flavour labels are illegible, the order is shuffled, and the legal text is unreadable.

A jams the chip row and CTA against the bottom edge with almost no margin, the legal text is a sliver crammed beside the last chip, and the small can is pinned to the top-left. B gives the can more presence and centres the CTA and chip row under the headline with bottom breathing room. But B floats the legal line on its own in empty space at mid-right, an arbitrary placement, and the CTA and chip text are still too small to read at this size.
